# Operate federal awards and workshares

The complete working record is a private USAspending workspace. Its original award editions, transaction captures, review revisions, source bytes, receiving records and prepared publications stay together in the original SQLite model. The browser and native merchant use that same model; the Applications controller opens the same saved directory.

## Install and open the product

Use the immutable source commit selected for this delivery. The maintained builder packages the **federal-awards** recipe:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --selection federal-awards --out /private/federal-awards-release
~~~

Retain the returned archive, archive SHA256 and build receipt. A resumed build uses the same output directory, source commit and selection with `--resume`. Inspect that existing operation with `--out DIRECTORY --status`.

The examples below use the installed `starforge` command. For a first installation, run the original source entry instead:

~~~sh
node /absolute/merchant-checkout/stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/runtime-install-cli.mjs --help
~~~

That source entry accepts the same `prepare`, `install`, `inspect` and `run` arguments shown after `starforge runtime-install`:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime \
  --archive /private/federal-awards-release/RETURNED_ARCHIVE.tgz \
  --sha256 RETURNED_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator
starforge runtime-install install --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime
starforge runtime-install inspect --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime --load --source
starforge runtime-install run --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime -- \
  usaspending-research --help
~~~

Use Node 22.16 or later and the original installer's actual dependency profile. A prepared runtime and the selected package remain paired; original install/resume/status commands preserve that operation. Follow [RUNTIME_INSTALL.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/RUNTIME_INSTALL.md) for its retained cache, offline installation and complete transfer options.

Create a private working parent and choose an original research directory. Research directories use mode 0700; connection and exported private files use mode 0600.

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research init --workspace /private/federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research serve --workspace /private/federal-awards --port 0
~~~

The browser prints an ephemeral loopback URL with its private session token. Open that URL in the operator's browser. Keep the URL with the private operating record. The research directory persists when the server stops; a later session opens the same workspace with a new live process identity.

## Bring in original award records

The browser can save official award queries, run their original pagination, enrich retained awards and select a working edition. Select the correct date semantics, prime-contract award types, agencies, NAICS/PSC and keywords for the research question. The capture retains the request, returned pages, continuation and coverage.

Existing source can be received without repeating its acquisition:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research import-detail \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards \
  --file /private/source/award.json --receipt /private/source/award.source.json \
  --name "Original selected award"

starforge usaspending-research import-collection \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards \
  --file /private/source/original-source-collection.json

starforge usaspending-research state --workspace /private/federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research browse \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --edition EDITION_ID --page 1 --limit 100
~~~

Choose the relevant import for the supplied original files. A collection keeps its original sibling files and hashes; copy the complete source collection when moving it. The result identifies the immutable edition. Select the award's generated `award_key` from that edition, preserving the original recipient and parent-recipient identities.

The award view separates awarding agency from funding agency, original source dates from observation time, and reported monetary fields from analyst notes. Use the source coverage shown beside any count or comparison.

## Capture and review funding actions

Select **Transactions & modifications** in the private browser or use the original award key and edition:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research tx-capture \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards \
  --edition EDITION_ID --key ORIGINAL_AWARD_KEY \
  --page-size 250 --max-rows 250000

starforge usaspending-research tx-state --workspace /private/federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research tx-summary \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID
starforge usaspending-research tx-browse \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID --page 1 --limit 100
~~~

The returned capture ID identifies this observation of that award's history. Continue original provider pagination until its terminal page. The workspace commits an accepted response and its normalized rows together. Provider retry timing, accepted pages, interrupted operations and retained row capacity remain visible in the same job and capture controls.

For an interrupted capture, resume that ID. If it reached the selected row capacity, read its current `updated_at`, increase capacity with `tx-capacity --capture ID --max-rows N --updated-at EXACT_TIME`, then use `tx-resume --capture ID`. The original request, pages and continuation remain the operation's inputs.

Already retained transaction pages can be imported with `tx-import --edition ID --key ORIGINAL_AWARD_KEY --file ORIGINAL_PAGES.json`. That file contains the complete native requests, receipts and base64 response bodies defined in [TRANSACTIONS.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/TRANSACTIONS.md).

Review chronological funding changes and federal fiscal-year subtotals beside the original agency action descriptions. The analysis preserves negative and zero obligations, unknown monetary values, duplicate occurrences and conflicts. Conflicting source identities remain unresolved until their original records support one interpretation. A later observation can be compared with `tx-compare --before CAPTURE_ID --after LATER_CAPTURE_ID`; coverage accompanies the added, changed and absent records.

## Save the full workshare

Save an assessment after the source capture completes. Include the actual fit, funding change, proposed workshare, deliverables, acceptance, owner, case URL and next action. Statuses are `researching`, `scope_match`, `review_with_owner` and `passed`. The two scope-oriented statuses require fit, proposed workshare, deliverables and acceptance.

A review file can contain:

~~~json
{
  "status": "scope_match",
  "fit": "Describe the specific delivery need supported by this award and the research.",
  "fundingChange": "Explain the original funding actions and their relevance to the proposed work.",
  "proposedWorkshare": "Name the complete implementation or service being offered.",
  "deliverables": "List the working software, editable source, operating materials and handover.",
  "acceptance": "Define the observable customer workflow and delivery completion.",
  "owner": "Relationship or delivery owner",
  "caseUrl": "https://example.com/internal-case",
  "nextAction": "Record the concrete action agreed by the relationship owner.",
  "notes": ""
}
~~~

Save it with the current review revision. The first review uses revision zero:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research tx-review \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID \
  --revision 0 --file /private/workshare-review.json

starforge usaspending-research tx-brief \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID \
  --out /private/delivery/workshare.md
~~~

The store binds the saved assessment to the retained source fingerprint and preserves its revision history. Keep commercial price, delivery timing and acceptance grounded in the proposed workshare. The prime award's reported contract values describe the original award.

## Prepare a dossier and complete editable delivery

Receive the selected original award edition into a research dossier using `usaspending-dossier receive`. The original dossier holds the research question, source observations, findings and citations. Its complete portable JSON preserves source blobs and revisions. [DOSSIER.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/DOSSIER.md) gives the original create, question, receive, finding, export and reopen commands.

For a full working handover, export the original workspace and transaction capture:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research backup \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --out /private/delivery/complete-workspace.json
starforge usaspending-research tx-export \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID \
  --include-reviews --out /private/delivery/transaction-capture.json
starforge usaspending-research tx-csv \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --capture CAPTURE_ID \
  --spreadsheet --out /private/delivery/transactions.csv
~~~

The JSON exports retain original receiving information. CSV and Markdown support reading and review. The [receiving guide](RECEIVING.md) follows the actual customer workflow through restoration, source import, dossier reopening and the original native continuations.

## Operate the native merchant

Create an existing private research directory and a mode-0600 connection file. A minimal connection selects that same workspace:

~~~json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.usaspending-workspace-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "federal": {
      "label": "Federal awards and workshares",
      "directory": "/private/federal-awards",
      "operator": "Federal research operator"
    }
  }
}
~~~

Initialize the original merchant configuration:

~~~sh
starforge merchant-mcp init-usaspending-workspaces \
  --dir /private/federal-awards-mcp \
  --connection /private/federal-awards-connection.json \
  --name "Federal awards and workshares"
~~~

Connect the original merchant stdio server to that configuration through its existing MCP instructions. The selected provider is `usa-spending-workspaces`. Call `merchant_usaspending_workspaces`, then `merchant_usaspending_open` for alias `federal`. An open instance returns the original research browser and dossier browser.

The transaction tool family provides inventory, capture, capacity, summary, rows, comparison, review saving and original source access. The existing source-import, job, pause, export and retained-file tools complete the same operation. Page inventories with their returned snapshot and next offset; retain the original export ID and offset through a long file transfer or connection restart.

Connection source kinds `transaction-pages` and `transactions` receive original pages and complete portable captures. The full connection declarations and tool arguments are in [USASPENDING-WORKSPACE.md](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/USASPENDING-WORKSPACE.md).

## Publish a reviewed award dataset when needed

Choose the immutable award edition to publish. The original merchant preparation projects public award fields into an immutable dataset bundle and keeps its source provenance:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research merchant-prepare \
  --workspace /private/federal-awards --edition EDITION_ID
starforge usaspending-research merchant-preview --bundle RETURNED_BUNDLE_DIRECTORY
~~~

For the payment-backed service, prepare with the original `--payment PAYMENT.json` and `--origin HTTPS_ORIGIN` together. Serve the retained bundle with `merchant-serve --bundle DIRECTORY` and the selected facilitator settings. The original offer, query, public schema and customer delivery interfaces remain the SF30/SF88/SF100 workflow. Receive an existing finalized customer delivery with `adopt-delivery --directory FINALIZED_DELIVERY_DIRECTORY`.

## Save a managed application

Attach the original READY runtime in the runtime workspace. In **Applications**, select **Federal awards and workshares**, choose the private research folder and optional receiving folder, review the selection, and save it. The shared save action creates approved new private directories. Start review then reopens that selection and launches the source-owned application.

Open the retained application URL. Stop from the same saved application and reopen it to continue the original awards, transactions, assessments and receiving history. The launcher and startup observer verify the same workspace and live process before the URL is retained. The full [application guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/APPLICATION.md) covers the original controller's operations.

# Federal awards and workshares

This product turns original federal award records and funding actions into a saved research workspace, a complete prime workshare, and a portable customer dossier. The operator browser, native merchant tools and managed application share the same private workspace. Original source pages, award editions, transaction history and assessment revisions remain available when another operator receives and reopens the work.

## Complete a workshare

1. Import retained original award records, or save and run an official USAspending query.
2. Select the prime award and inspect the original recipient, awarding agency, funding agency, dates and separately reported monetary fields.
3. Capture the award's transaction history. Review modification numbers, chronological funding changes and federal fiscal-year totals against each action's original source page.
4. Save the proposed workshare, deliverables, acceptance, relationship owner and next action against the completed source capture.
5. Export the complete private workspace and workshare brief, or receive the original award edition into a dossier with its question, findings and source citations.
6. Reopen the delivered workspace through the same browser, native merchant connection or saved Applications entry. When a reviewed award dataset is part of the service, prepare and operate it through the original SF30 merchant and receive its finalized customer delivery.

The original [USAspending transaction contract](https://github.com/fedspendingtransparency/usaspending-api/blob/master/usaspending_api/api_contracts/contracts/v2/transactions.md) supplies the provider fields and pagination. Source amounts retain their exact decimal values. Award obligations, transaction obligations, exercised contract value, all-options value and outlays remain distinct throughout analysis and delivery.

## Install the selected product

The maintained distribution selection is **federal-awards**. Build it from one immutable commit of this repository:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/distribution/build.mjs \
  --repo /absolute/merchant-checkout --ref ORIGINAL_COMMIT \
  --selection federal-awards --out /private/federal-awards-release
~~~

The original build receipt identifies the package archive and its SHA256. Use those returned values with the maintained installer:

~~~sh
starforge runtime-install prepare \
  --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime \
  --archive /private/federal-awards-release/RETURNED_ARCHIVE.tgz \
  --sha256 RETURNED_ARCHIVE_SHA256 \
  --native --feature schema --feature openapi --feature mcp --operator

starforge runtime-install install --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime
starforge runtime-install inspect --dir /private/federal-awards-runtime --load --source
~~~

Use Linux and Node 22.16 or later, the original Git checkout, and the toolchain required by the selected runtime dependencies. The [operating guide](OPERATING.md) covers first installation, the source command before an installed `starforge` is available, private workspace setup, the complete analyst workflow and native merchant operation. The [receiving guide](RECEIVING.md) covers complete editable handover and the original native receiving programs.

## Open the saved work

From the installed product:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research init --workspace /private/federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research serve --workspace /private/federal-awards --port 0
~~~

Open the returned private browser URL. Use **Transactions & modifications** or an award's **Research transaction history** action to work from its original edition.

For managed operation, attach the READY runtime in the original runtime workspace, open **Applications**, and select **Federal awards and workshares**. Save the private research folder and optional customer delivery folder, then use its reviewed start, open, stop and reopen actions. The [application guide](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/APPLICATION.md) describes the full source-owned launcher and saved application lifecycle.

# Receive and reopen federal award work

A complete delivery includes the selected source package and the working research record. Choose the original complete workspace, portable award/transaction records, and dossier exports that the recipient needs. Keep the private assessments and session URLs inside the intended delivery.

## Delivery contents

| Artifact | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Selected federal-awards package, its original build receipt and SHA256 | Install the same source-owned commands, application and native merchant |
| complete-workspace.json | Restore the full award and transaction workspace, original pages, review history and receiving state |
| transaction-capture.json with reviews when selected | Receive one complete award history into the matching retained award edition |
| Original award edition or its complete award/detail source collection | Establish the original award and provenance for separate transaction receiving |
| Original transaction response and receipt exports | Inspect the exact source request, response, observation and identity |
| workshare.md and transactions.csv | Read the workshare and examine spreadsheet-safe transaction rows |
| Complete dossier JSON and optional HTML/Markdown exports | Reopen the original research question, sources, findings, citations and revision history |
| Prepared merchant bundle or finalized customer delivery when part of the work | Continue the original publication and customer receiving workflow |

Retain the complete original source collections, including files referenced by their manifests. Exported JSON and immutable dataset bundles preserve their own source bindings. Output paths are create-only; use a new destination for another delivery edition.

## Restore the complete working research record

Install the selected package as described in [OPERATING.md](OPERATING.md). Choose a new private workspace and restore the original full backup:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research restore \
  --workspace /private/received-federal-awards \
  --file /private/delivery/complete-workspace.json

starforge usaspending-research state --workspace /private/received-federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research serve --workspace /private/received-federal-awards --port 0
~~~

Open the new private browser URL and inspect the retained award edition, selected award, completed transaction capture and saved assessment. Source observation times and original monetary values remain attached to that research record. A reopened server has its own live instance while the saved workspace identity persists.

Full restore verifies the original source bytes and their page/row bindings before committing. It also supports original backups created before the additive transaction tables existed.

## Receive a transaction capture into an existing original award workspace

Receive or import the original award edition first, preserving its award row and provenance. Select that resulting edition and then receive the portable transaction capture:

~~~sh
starforge usaspending-research tx-receive \
  --workspace /private/received-federal-awards \
  --file /private/delivery/transaction-capture.json \
  --edition RECEIVING_EDITION_ID --include-reviews

starforge usaspending-research tx-state --workspace /private/received-federal-awards
starforge usaspending-research tx-summary \
  --workspace /private/received-federal-awards --capture RETURNED_CAPTURE_ID
~~~

The receiver checks the copied award row, exact native request/response pages, projected transaction occurrences, coverage and source fingerprint. Included workshare receiving is explicit. The original review provenance remains attached to the receiving record; replay reuses the retained receiving result according to the original receiver.

Use a full workspace restore when the delivery needs all original award editions, source history and assessments together.

## Reopen the original dossier

The complete dossier JSON carries its original question, findings, citations, source observations and blobs. Reopen it into the new private dossier store using the original command:

~~~sh
starforge research-dossiers reopen \
  --store /private/received-dossiers \
  --file /private/delivery/complete.research.json
~~~

Open the dossier with `starforge usaspending-dossier open --store /private/received-dossiers`. Recover a selected original award edition with the source-signature command in [DOSSIER.md](../../stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/DOSSIER.md). This keeps source receiving and the written workshare in one customer workflow.

## Receive through the native merchant

Declare the existing source files in the original workspace connection. A portable transaction source uses `kind: transactions`; retained native request/receipt/response pages use `kind: transaction-pages`. The source-import tool accepts the original award edition and explicit review receiving.

Use the original export and retained-file tools for large deliveries. Preserve the export ID, expected snapshot and returned next offset. After closing and reopening the same owner, continue that original export from its retained offset, receive the complete capture, and reopen the receiving workspace. See the complete [native merchant guide](../../stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/USASPENDING-WORKSPACE.md).

## Run the original end-to-end receiving programs

These programs consume an actual original source packet and the complete source files. They exercise the maintained application and saved workspaces. Retain the full output directories, original inputs, stdout and stderr with the receiving operation.

From the source root of the selected product, run the original award and transaction journey:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/transactions/run-native.mjs \
  --source /private/original-source-packet.json \
  --out /private/receiving/native
~~~

The packet contains the complete original award/detail receipt and transaction request/response records expected by the maintained runner. Its native output includes the working award workspace, original capture, private assessment, transaction exports, complete workspace backup, restored workspace, received capture and receiving-result.json.

Continue that same output through the original merchant owner:

~~~sh
node stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/examples/usaspending-transactions-native.mjs \
  --received /private/receiving/native \
  --out /private/receiving/mcp-native \
  --operation SCF-USASPENDING-AWARD-TRANSACTIONS-64B7-20261012
~~~

The MCP continuation uses the original job controller, snapshot-paged timeline, workshare review and all six complete transaction export formats. It closes and reopens the owner during a retained-file transfer, receives the portable capture, replays receiving and reopens the saved result. Its operation.json retains progress; continuation uses the same operation ID and output directory.

Run the original source-owned application on that same received workspace:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/application-native.mjs \
  --received /private/receiving/native \
  --out /private/receiving/applications-source
~~~

For this source mode, the original source root is the `source` child of its release directory. The selected runtime naturally has that layout. The program reads the source-owned provider registry, launches the real original server, receives its authenticated startup identity and browser assets, verifies saved transactions and assessment, stops with SIGTERM, and reopens the same workspace. It also opens a new workspace, restores the complete original backup and reopens the restored work.

To complete the shared Applications lifecycle, supply the original READY runtime:

~~~sh
node stellar/scf-starforge-20261009/sf30-seller-sdk/usaspending/application-native.mjs \
  --received /private/receiving/native \
  --out /private/receiving/applications-managed \
  --runtime /private/federal-awards-runtime
~~~

That mode uses the maintained runtime inspector and runtime workspace model: attach, application review/save, original adoption, fresh start preparation, managed worker, authenticated private browser, stop, controller reopen and saved application reopen. It covers an existing original workspace and a new workspace whose approved directories are created by the original save flow. Each application receiving run takes its own new output directory.

The original complete receiving directories provide the working customer result and the source errors needed to repair an interrupted run. Preserve them with the operation so further work continues against the same original record.

# Source-owned merchant providers

A merchant provider contributes its own tool metadata, host configuration reader,
runtime factory, request limit, lifecycle settings, instructions and setup hook.
The existing distribution contributions select these modules. The existing
MerchantProviderOwners loader constructs a configured runtime only when it is
used, retains its original dependencies, and closes the same owner.

## Inspect the installed providers

Run the maintained commands from a source checkout or installed distribution:

```sh
starforge merchant-providers list
starforge merchant-providers inspect openapi-workspaces
starforge merchant-providers init openapi-workspaces --options /private/openapi-setup.json
```

The setup JSON contains the original initializer's options. For the existing
OpenAPI initializer, a complete example is:

```json
{
  "directory": "/private/openapi-merchant",
  "connection": "/private/openapi-connection.json",
  "name": "OpenAPI merchant"
}
```

The provider hook calls the existing initializer. Its source configuration,
workspace identities, native setup and recovery behavior stay with that
implementation. The legacy init-* commands and exported initializer functions
remain available. Direct merchant MCP commands also expose
providers list|inspect and init-provider ID --options FILE.

## Register a provider

Add merchantProviders to the component's existing contribution JSON, or add its
own contribution in distribution/contributions. The contribution schema and
ownership rules are the same as commands, exports, browser assets and
applicationProviders:

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.merchant-distribution-contribution.v1",
  "id": "merchant-provider-openapi-workspaces",
  "description": "Original OpenAPI workspace MCP provider",
  "merchantProviders": {
    "openapi-workspaces": "stellar-forge/mcp-merchant-operator/providers/openapi-workspaces.mjs"
  }
}
```

Keep the component and supportFiles declarations for the native implementation,
dynamic imports, maintained data and browser assets. The builder selects each
declared provider module explicitly and follows its real static ESM imports.
It reads declarations from one immutable Git snapshot and does not execute
provider code while building.

Provider IDs use lower-case words separated by hyphens. The family is the stable
merchantToolFamily value, so existing camelCase family and configuration keys
continue to work. One source owns each ID, family, configuration key and raw host
input. The composer reports conflicting contribution paths. The runtime rejects
duplicate tools, unknown ownership dependencies and dependency cycles.

## Provider module

The declaration imports metadata only. The complete maintained OpenAPI example
is providers/openapi-workspaces.mjs; all original families now use the same
interface:

```js
import { defineMerchantProvider, MERCHANT_PROVIDER_SCHEMA } from '../provider-contract.mjs';
import { openapiWorkspaceTools } from '../catalog/openapi-workspace.mjs';

export default defineMerchantProvider({
  schema: MERCHANT_PROVIDER_SCHEMA,
  id: 'openapi-workspaces',
  family: 'openapiWorkspaces',
  title: 'OpenAPI merchant workspaces',
  configKey: 'openapiWorkspaces',
  configuration: {
    input: 'openapiWorkspaceConnection',
    privateExports: true,
    read: async (value, { hostPath }) =>
      (await import('../openapi-workspace.mjs'))
        .readOpenApiWorkspaceConfiguration(hostPath(value))
  },
  tools: openapiWorkspaceTools,
  load: () => import('../openapi-workspace.mjs'),
  create: (module, config, options) =>
    new module.MerchantOpenApiWorkspaces(config, options.openapi),
  initialize: async options =>
    (await import('../config.mjs')).initializeOpenApiWorkspaceMerchant(options)
});
```

New sources provide their own initialize implementation in their own setup
module. They do not add a per-family branch to config.mjs, catalog.mjs,
operator.mjs, instructions.mjs or serve.mjs. The package exports the contract
and paired TypeScript declaration as ./merchant-provider, and the registry
reader as ./merchant-providers.

The factory receives the loaded native module, the original normalized merchant
configuration, caller-selected runtime options, and already-created dependency
owners. The common options.environment contains the environment selected by
startMerchantMcp; providers pass it to their original native client or process
owner. Existing per-provider options remain available. A source can combine its
common environment and optional own options inside its factory without adding
a family branch to the host server. It returns the original runtime object. Ordinary provider tools use its
existing call(name, args), summary and close() interfaces.

Trusted JavaScript callers of `startMerchantMcp` may pass `providerOptions`,
a plain object whose keys are the runtime option names consumed by their
selected provider declarations. The host passes its common `environment` and
all existing nested defaults first, then spreads `providerOptions` over them.
A supplied top-level key replaces that entire option value; nested provider
records are not deep-merged. For example:

```js
const merchant = await startMerchantMcp({
  configPath, environment,
  providerOptions: { nws: { environment, fetchImpl: sourceFetch } },
});
```

This startup argument can carry existing native functions and handles. It is
not an MCP request field or a path for remote code selection. The explicit
startup authentication and OAuth arguments keep their existing behavior;
overriding provider runtime options affects the provider factories. Omitting
`providerOptions` retains the original defaults.

## Configuration and ordering

configuration.input is the original top-level host input, such as
openapiWorkspaceConnection. The merchant reader validates the union of these
inputs and the five common merchant fields. It calls only configured readers;
an omitted input becomes null under configKey. A provider with configKey: null
uses the common merchant configuration and has no separate reader.

The read hook receives the original input value and context containing base,
config and hostPath(value). hostPath resolves the original reference against the
merchant configuration file. The reader performs the component's existing
validation; it does not accept executable paths through MCP tool arguments.

configuration.dependencies lists family names whose normalized configuration
must already exist. For example, ArcGIS reads its declared publishers before
binding its own workspace. Runtime dependencies use the separate top-level
dependencies array and preserve the original borrowing owners. Both graphs
are validated before work starts.

order preserves runtime inventory order. catalogOrder controls family tool
order. Existing declarations retain their original tool order, schemas,
configuration names and request limits. maxRequestBytes contributes the
component's original incoming request limit; the host uses the largest
configured value and its common 128 KiB floor. configuration.privateExports
keeps the existing private customer-export-directory requirement.

## Native concurrency and shutdown

These fields use the existing MerchantProviderOwners lifecycle:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| concurrency: host | Mutations use the original host change lock. This is the default. |
| concurrency: provider | The original provider owns its concurrency and recovery. |
| concurrentTools | Exact native cancel/stop controls that remain available during a host-serialized mutation. Every named tool must belong to this provider. |
| shutdown: drain | Finish accepted host calls, then close this original runtime. This is the default. |
| shutdown: provider | The original close can cancel and drain accepted native work; begin it after accepted calls enter the provider. |
| requestClose(runtime) | Signal the original owner's cancellation method without replacing that owner. |
| dependencies | Borrowing providers finish before the owners they borrow. An incomplete close retains the original handles for an explicit close retry. |

Declare the behavior implemented by the original runtime. A broad set of control
tools is not a substitute for its native cancellation and operation recovery.
The host keeps accepted call and shutdown metadata in its original status view.

## Instructions and source identity

instructions contains original guidance sections with order, text, and either a
prefix or exact tool selector. The host selects them from its advertised tools.
The migrated original always-present sections preserve their previous behavior.
New provider guidance should use its own tool prefix.

The runtime reads the same complete contribution inventory as the package
builder. It resolves modules inside the selected original source, checks
regular-file identity while reading and loading, and verifies installed
provider bytes against the distribution manifest. Inspection reports the
original provider path, SHA256, byte count and owning contributions.

Adding or changing a source declaration takes effect when the host starts from
that complete source. A running operator keeps its selected modules and native
owners for the lifetime of that process.

| Tool | Operation |
| --- | --- |
| `merchant_sources` | Inspect configured files or a saved API package, with public routes, payment choices, backend mappings and input hashes. |
| `merchant_stage` | Compile an alias to a new immutable release ID, retaining the original upstream snapshot when configured. |
| `merchant_inspect` | Verify the original retained release and inspect its exact digest and terms. |
| `merchant_compare` | Compare route, price and application changes with the active or specified previous release. |
| `merchant_activate` | Select a release using its digest and the current selection generation. |
| `merchant_start` | Start that selection through the original foreground seller launcher. |
| `merchant_status` | Inspect selected and running releases, history, readiness, and which process owns the seller. |
| `merchant_catalog` | Read actual seller health, offers and OpenAPI from that process-owned instance. |
| `merchant_client_export` | Export the original JS client, TypeScript declarations, OpenAPI and guide into a new named customer directory with a durable completion receipt. |
| `merchant_client_export_status` | Verify the retained customer files after a lost response, seller shutdown or provider restart. |
| `merchant_client_export_adopt` | Explicitly retain the inspected digest of an original legacy five-file export without regenerating it. |
| `merchant_client_export_manifest` | Review the original saved completion receipt and exact manifest identity. |
| `merchant_client_export_file` | Retrieve SHA-pinned chunks of one original customer payload or its receipt. |
| `merchant_client_export_file_release` | Release only the selected temporary read snapshot. |
| `merchant_rollback` | Select an exact retained release through original rollback history. |
| `merchant_restart` | Drain the owned instance and start the selected version. |
| `merchant_stop` | Gracefully drain only the instance owned by this MCP process. |
| `merchant_discovery_status` | Compare a retained release with current signed catalog listings and reconcile the original history. |
| `merchant_discovery_review` | Review publication of the running release or withdrawal of one listed route; no key access or signature. |
| `merchant_discovery_apply` | Apply this host's exact latest review through the original signed catalog batch or withdrawal. |
| `merchant_cache_status` | Inspect the current original per-route cache policy, occupancy and source counters. |
| `merchant_cache_invalidate` | Invalidate one route or all caches on the exact seller instance owned by this MCP host. |

For complete signed publication, updates, withdrawal and cache operation, follow
the [merchant operating workflow](./OPERATIONS.md). Initialization accepts
`--catalog CATALOG_CONNECTION_JSON`, or an existing host configuration can
reference that private connection with `catalogConnection`. The original
catalog directory and signing-key file stay on the host. These tools use both
the existing HTTP provider and its existing stdio entrypoint.

For example, call `merchant_sources` with `{"source":"initial"}`, then
`merchant_stage` with `{"source":"initial","id":"release-1"}`. Inspect and
compare `release-1`; use its returned `digest` as `expectedDigest`, and the
current status or comparison `generation` as `expectedGeneration` when
activating it. Supply a short reason. `merchant_start` takes the resulting
selection generation and the same release digest. It returns a status with
`operator.instanceId`; use that exact instance for catalog, client export, stop
or restart. Client export also takes a new ID such as `customer-1`.

The [customer SDK delivery workflow](./CLIENT_EXPORTS.md) completes export, lost-response
inspection, explicit legacy adoption, download/resume and original generated-client
use. `merchant-mcp inspect-client` reviews the saved receipt; `download-client`
retains the five exact payloads locally with durable checkpoints. It remains
available after the original seller stops and does not run generated code.

Changing selection leaves the currently running seller on its original release.
Status reports `RESTART_REQUIRED`. Inspect the comparison and call
`merchant_restart` with the current generation, target digest and owned instance
to apply it. Rollback follows the same sequence and preserves the original
release history. If startup fails after a restart's stop, the seller stays
stopped; `merchant_status` records the failure and selected version.

Only one mutating tool runs at a time within this operator. The original release
store's generation and process locks preserve changes made by other consoles.
An existing process owned by another console is visible but cannot be stopped
or adopted through MCP. A request interrupted after a side effect is reconciled
by inspecting the original release ID, generation or instance; the server does
not automatically replay tools. Customer output publication is exclusive, so a
repeated export ID cannot replace an existing delivery.

Closing MCP waits for its accepted mutation and drains the original seller it
owns. A crash preserves the existing release store and original process record;
the original SF82 recovery behavior determines whether a seller is still alive.
Private response content and handler paths are omitted from normal release
results. Exact public payment terms, application hashes and original native or
challenge-only mode remain visible.

```json
{
  "schema": "stellar-forge.usaspending-workspace-connection.v1",
  "workspaces": {
    "federal": {
      "label": "Federal award research",
      "directory": "/private/award-research/research",
      "dossierDirectory": "/private/award-research/dossiers",
      "operator": "Federal research operator",
      "sources": {

          "kind": "collection",
          "file": "/private/source/source/recent-ai-v2-details.json"
        },

        }
      },
      "deliveries": {
        "original-buyer": "/private/original-buyer/delivery"
      },
      "merchant": {
        "defaultLimit": 50,
        "maxLimit": 100

```

| Kind | Host declaration | Native reader |
| --- | --- | --- |
| collection | file; optional SHA256 | Original capture plus retained award-detail collection |
| capture | file; optional SHA256 | Original provider request, response and receipt pages |
| detail | file and receipt; optional SHA256 | One original award-detail response and HTTP receipt |
| workspace | file; optional SHA256 | Complete research backup, restored into an empty workspace |
| dossier | file; optional SHA256 | Complete portable dossier with revision and blob validation |

The connection file uses mode 0600; private directories use mode 0700. Source
paths are host configuration. Tools select the declared aliases and original
record IDs. Source collections retain their existing sibling-file and SHA256

## Complete the cited dossier

The dossier browser and MCP use the same original private store, immutable
revision files and content-addressed source blobs. Every write follows the
original expected-revision checks.

1. Create a dossier with `dossier_create`.
2. Add questions with `dossier_question`. Retain their returned original IDs.
3. Receive a complete award edition under one question with
   `dossier_receive`, passing its current dossier revision.
4. Read the sources section with `dossier`. Each source retains its
   question citations, original response components and source identity.
5. Select supporting, contradicting or background evidence with
   `dossier_evidence`. Use an occurrence ID for a question-specific
   selection, or the original source ID for the native source selection.
6. Write the actual finding with `dossier_finding`, its question ID and
   original cited source IDs. The original engine validates the question binding.
7. Export the complete portable JSON, Markdown and HTML report.

Receiving preserves the full edition, original capture pages, detailed response
bodies and any original native buyer archives. Receiving the same edition under
a different question produces that question's native source bindings.
An interrupted multi-component receive retains its progress on the original
error, and repeating the same selection uses the bridge's original replay logic.

`dossier_update` edits the title or description.
`dossier_question` edits a saved question's text, notes and status.
`dossier_finding` edits a saved finding using its original finding ID.
`dossier_compare` compares retained revisions.
For stable historical section paging, pass the original revision returned by
the dossier read.

A portable dossier can be declared as a source handle on a receiving workspace
and reopened with `source_import`. The original engine checks every
revision, blob, question, selection and finding reference before reopening.

## Export every byte and resume later

`export` creates a complete retained file through the original serializer.
It returns the export kind, immutable SHA256 export ID, exact byte count, MIME
type and native selection. The export is atomically retained in the merchant's
private customer-export directory.

| Kind | Required selection |
| --- | --- |
| edition-json | editionId; optional includeReviews |
| edition-csv | editionId |
| workspace | None |
| source-page | captureId and page |
| brief | editionId and awardKey |
| comparison | before and after edition IDs |
| dossier-json, dossier-md, dossier-html | dossierId |
| merchant-csv, merchant-dataset, merchant-source, merchant-bundle, merchant-seller | merchantId |

The complete edition JSON includes original source bytes and source coverage.
The full workspace backup includes every original table and retained provider
response. Workspace export requires its active provider work to be finished or
paused. Analyst review inclusion is selected explicitly for edition JSON.

Use `file_read` with the same workspace alias, kind and export ID.
The shared retained-file reader returns exact base64 chunks and
`nextOffset`; continue until it is null. Its response includes the file
SHA256, total bytes and read ID. Every read checks the retained export's bytes
against its content-addressed ID.

The original complete file survives read-session expiry and application
restart. Resume with the same kind, export ID and byte offset, omitting an
expired read ID. `file_release` releases only the temporary read snapshot.

Use `close` with the current instance ID when finished. Reopening the
same configured alias retains the original research ID, dossiers, source
records, merchant packages, native delivery archives and complete exported
files.

## Complete award transaction history

The transaction tools operate the original AwardWorkspace transaction store in
the same SQLite database. Acquisition runs through the research browser's
existing job controller. The original job, pause, instance ownership and shutdown
tools also govern transaction captures.

Select the original award in its retained edition before capturing transactions.
The provider's transaction ID is separate from the award ID. Action descriptions
retain the agency's text; funding direction and exact obligation changes come
from the original monetary fields. Decimal source values remain strings, and
nullable loan values remain distinct from obligations.

| Native tool | Complete operation |
| --- | --- |
| transaction_inventory | Page retained captures or workshare reviews, optionally for one award |
| transaction_capture | Start an award capture or resume its original capture ID |
| transaction_capacity | Change paused row capacity using its exact updated_at |
| transaction_summary | Read exact totals and review, then page fiscal years, conflicts or duplicate occurrences |
| transaction_rows | Browse the retained timeline with search and date filters |
| transaction_compare | Compare original captures and page added, changed, absent, unresolved or conflicting source records |
| transaction_review_save | Save the source-bound workshare assessment with its expected revision |
| transaction_source | Read original request, receipt, observation time and response identity |

Every name in this table has the prefix
`merchant_usaspending_`. Existing `source_import`, `export`,
`file_read`, `file_release`, `job`, `status`, `pause` and
`close` complete the same workflow.

### Capture and recover the original operation

Call `transaction_capture` with `editionId` and `awardKey`.
Optional `pageSize` selects 1–5000 official transactions per page; `maxRows`
selects the retained capacity up to 250000 rows. The returned job belongs to
the existing research browser. Inspect that original job with
`merchant_usaspending_job`. Its durable transaction capture ID also appears in
the workspace status and transaction inventory.

To continue an interrupted operation, call `transaction_capture` with only its
original `captureId`. Accepted pages, response bytes and provider continuation
remain attached to that capture. `merchant_usaspending_pause` accepts the
original job ID or capture ID. For a capacity change, read the capture's
`updated_at` in its summary and pass it as `expectedUpdatedAt` to
`transaction_capacity` before resuming.

Transaction inventories and summary/comparison sections use the existing
offset, limit and snapshot protocol. Continue with the returned `nextOffset`
and `expectedSnapshot`. Timeline rows use the model's page/limit protocol.
Page one also returns a timeline snapshot; pass it as `expectedSnapshot` on
later pages with the same filters and limit. If an active capture advances,
reopen page one with its new snapshot.

The summary retains source coverage beside the calculated totals. Conflicted
source IDs remain unresolved in comparisons. A fiscal-year count is unknown
when conflicting dates span fiscal years; `possible_transactions` is that
year's candidate upper bound. The full captured data remains available in the
transaction JSON export.

### Receive exact source and portable captures

Add existing canonical files to the normal workspace connection's `sources`
object:

```json
{
  "original-transactions": {
    "kind": "transaction-pages",
    "file": "/private/source/original-transaction-pages.json"
  },
  "portable-transactions": {
    "kind": "transactions",
    "file": "/private/receiving/transaction-capture.json"
  }
}
```

An optional `sha256` pins either complete declared file. The retained-page file
contains an array, or an object with `pages`, whose entries retain the native
`request`, complete `receipt` and `responseBase64`. The original store verifies
the endpoint, request body, response bytes, observation times, contiguous pages
and selected award before accepting them.

Call `merchant_usaspending_source_import` with
`source=original-transactions`, the receiving `editionId` and original
`awardKey`. Optional `maxRows` selects capacity for that exact retained capture.
This adds the original provider pages through the same native importer.

For a complete portable capture, call the same source-import tool with
`source=portable-transactions`. An optional `editionId` selects the already
received original award edition; otherwise the packet retains its original
edition selection. Set `includeReview=true` to receive the included workshare
assessment with its original source provenance. The original receiver checks
the award row, page receipts, projected transactions, complete coverage and
source fingerprint before accepting the packet. Receive the original award
edition first. Workspace backups also retain transaction tables, pages and
reviews through the existing full-workspace serializer and restore path.

### Preserve the complete workshare and every output byte

Save a review with `transaction_review_save`, its `captureId`,
`expectedRevision`, and `review`. The statuses are `researching`,
`scope_match`, `review_with_owner` and `passed`. Available fields are
`fit`, `fundingChange`, `proposedWorkshare`, `deliverables`,
`acceptance`, `owner`, `caseUrl`, `nextAction` and `notes`.
The native store binds the review to the completed capture's source fingerprint.
The two scope-oriented statuses require the actual fit, workshare, deliverables
and acceptance.

The existing `merchant_usaspending_export` now supports:

| Kind | Selection and contents |
| --- | --- |
| transaction-json | captureId; complete provider pages, receipts, projected rows and coverage; optional includeReviews |
| transaction-csv | captureId; complete spreadsheet-safe transaction rows |
| transaction-source | captureId and page; exact original response bytes |
| transaction-source-receipt | captureId and page; original request, HTTP receipt and response identity |
| transaction-comparison | before and after capture IDs; every native comparison section |
| transaction-brief | captureId; original award brief plus transaction history and workshare assessment |

Each export uses the existing immutable export ID and complete-file reader.
Retain its kind, export ID and returned next offset through every read. Release
the read snapshot after receiving the full file. After closing and reopening
the owned workspace, resume the same export ID and offset. The same exact
transaction JSON can then be declared as a receiving source and imported into
the original award workspace.
